title: Psalms 78
paragraphs: ¹ Listen, my people, to my instruction; lean in to the words I speak. ² I will open my mouth in a parable; I will pour out the deep lessons of the past — ³ what we have heard and known, what our ancestors have told us. ⁴ We will not hide them from their children; we will tell the next generation the praiseworthy deeds of the LORD, his power, and the wonders he has done. ⁵ For he established a decree in Jacob and set up a law in Israel, which he commanded our ancestors to teach their children,

⁶ so that the next generation would know them, even the children yet to be born, who would in turn tell their own children — ⁷ so that they would put their trust in God and not forget his deeds, but keep his commands. ⁸ They would not be like their ancestors — a stubborn and rebellious generation, whose hearts were not loyal to God, whose spirits were not faithful to him. ⁹ The men of Ephraim, though armed with bows, turned back on the day of battle. ¹⁰ They did not keep God's covenant and refused to live by his law.

¹¹ They forgot what he had done — the wonders he had shown them. ¹² He did miraculous things in the sight of their ancestors in the land of Egypt, in the region of Zoan. ¹³ He divided the sea and led them through; the waters stood up like walls. ¹⁴ He guided them with the cloud by day and with a fiery light all through the night. ¹⁵ He split the rocks in the desert and gave them water as plentiful as the deep ocean.

¹⁶ He brought streams out of a rocky crag and made water flow down like rivers. ¹⁷ But they continued to sin against him, rebelling against the Most High in the desert. ¹⁸ They deliberately tested God, demanding the food they craved. ¹⁹ They spoke against God, saying, "Can God spread a table in the desert? ²⁰ Yes, he struck the rock, and water gushed out, and streams flowed freely — but can he give bread too? Can he supply meat for his people?"

²¹ When the LORD heard this, he was furious; a fire broke out against Jacob, and his anger flared against Israel, ²² because they did not believe in God or trust in his salvation — ²³ even though he had commanded the skies above and opened the doors of the heavens, ²⁴ raining down manna for them to eat and giving them the grain of heaven. ²⁵ Mortals ate the bread of angels; he sent them all the food they could eat.

²⁶ He let loose the east wind from the heavens and by his power drove the south wind. ²⁷ He rained meat down on them like dust, and birds like sand on the seashore. ²⁸ He made them fall inside their camp, all around their tents. ²⁹ They ate and were well satisfied, for he gave them what they craved. ³⁰ But before they had turned away from what they desired — before the food was even gone from their mouths —

³¹ the anger of God rose against them; he put to death the strongest among them, cutting down the young men of Israel. ³² In spite of all this, they kept on sinning; in spite of his wonders, they did not believe. ³³ So he ended their days in futility and their years in terror. ³⁴ Whenever he slew them, they would seek him; they eagerly turned back to God. ³⁵ They remembered that God was their Rock, that God Most High was their Redeemer.

³⁶ But they only flattered him with their mouths; they lied to him with their tongues. ³⁷ Their hearts were not loyal to him; they were not faithful to his covenant. ³⁸ Yet he was merciful; he forgave their sins and did not destroy them. Time and again he held back his anger and did not stir up his full wrath. ³⁹ He remembered that they were but flesh, a passing wind that does not return. ⁴⁰ How often they rebelled against him in the desert and grieved him in the wasteland!

⁴¹ Again and again they tested God, provoking the Holy One of Israel. ⁴² They did not remember his power — the day he redeemed them from the oppressor, ⁴³ how he displayed his signs in Egypt, his wonders in the region of Zoan. ⁴⁴ He turned their rivers to blood; they could not drink from their streams. ⁴⁵ He sent swarms of flies that devoured them, and frogs that devastated them.

⁴⁶ He handed their crops over to caterpillars and their labor to the locust. ⁴⁷ He destroyed their vines with hail and their sycamore trees with frost. ⁴⁸ He gave their cattle up to the hail and their flocks to bolts of lightning. ⁴⁹ He unleashed his fierce anger upon them — wrath, indignation, and distress — sending a host of destroying angels among them. ⁵⁰ He cleared a path for his anger; he did not spare their lives from death but gave them over to plague.

⁵¹ He struck down every firstborn in Egypt, the very best of their strength in the land of Ham. ⁵² But he led his own people out like sheep and guided them through the wilderness like a flock. ⁵³ He led them safely, and they had nothing to fear — the sea swallowed up their enemies. ⁵⁴ He brought them to the border of his holy land, to this mountain his own hand had claimed. ⁵⁵ He drove out nations before them, allotted their land by lot, and settled the tribes of Israel in their tents.

⁵⁶ Yet they tested and defied the Most High God and refused to keep his decrees. ⁵⁷ They turned back and betrayed him just like their ancestors — as unreliable as a faulty bow. ⁵⁸ They provoked him with their high places of worship and stirred his jealousy with their carved idols. ⁵⁹ When God heard this, he burned with fury and utterly rejected Israel. ⁶⁰ He abandoned the tabernacle at Shiloh, the tent he had pitched among people.

⁶¹ He let his strength go into captivity and his glory into enemy hands. ⁶² He handed his people over to the sword and unleashed his anger on his own inheritance. ⁶³ Fire consumed their young men, and their young women were left with no one to marry. ⁶⁴ Their priests fell by the sword, and their widows could not even weep. ⁶⁵ Then the LORD roused himself like someone waking from sleep, like a warrior shaking off the effects of wine.

⁶⁶ He struck his enemies from behind and put them to lasting shame. ⁶⁷ He rejected the tents of Joseph and did not choose the tribe of Ephraim. ⁶⁸ Instead he chose the tribe of Judah — Mount Zion, which he loved. ⁶⁹ He built his sanctuary as lofty as the heavens, as firm as the earth he established forever. ⁷⁰ He chose his servant David and took him from the sheepfolds.
⁷¹ From tending ewes nursing their young he brought him to shepherd Jacob his people and Israel his inheritance. ⁷² So David tended them with integrity of heart and guided them with skillful hands.
